page: Microsoft Azure E96pds_v7 is an ARM64 memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 96 dedicated compute cores built upon ARM architecture, delivering high thread capacity without simultaneous multithreading dependencies. Designed to handle large compute footprints, the architecture targets software environments compiled natively for 64-bit ARM.

System memory totals 768 GB, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio that fits data-dense environments. Complementing the memory tier is 5,669 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage. This substantial temporary storage volume provides high-throughput, low-latency scratch space, which reduces disk I/O bottlenecks when processing intermediate datasets or managing local swap partitions. The platform additionally supports Azure Premium Storage for durable, external disk attachments.

The use of ARM64 processors offers favorable compute density and operational efficiency compared to traditional x86 server classes running high-capacity memory footprints. The primary technical constraint involves binary compatibility, as the instance cannot run software reliant on x86-specific instruction sets or vector extensions. The instance profile is suited for memory-intensive applications, including large-scale relational databases, distributed caching layers, in-memory data processing frameworks, and enterprise business applications.
description: Microsoft Azure E96pds_v7 is an ARM64 memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 96 dedicated vCPUs and 768 GB of system memory. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the server provides an 8.0 GB per core memory allocation suited for data-intensive processing. In addition to its large memory footprint, the configuration bundles 5,669 GB of direct-attached NVMe solid-state storage alongside compatibility with Azure Premium Storage for persistent volumes. The underlying ARM64 architecture provides significant compute density and qualitative operating efficiency for large-scale operations. However, deploying to this instance requires software support for ARM64 instructions, precluding workloads that depend strictly on x86 SIMD extensions. The system is designed for in-memory databases, large-scale relational databases, real-time caching tiers, and memory-bound analytics workloads that benefit from high-density memory and fast local scratch storage.
